lessons.text: When a clause specifies a group of individuals with a condition such as 'covered under any other statutory social security schemes', do not write a rule for that condition.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions coverage under other schemes
lessons.review_note: Wrong: C03's reviewed rules exclude NPS, ESIC and EPFO members (three eq false rules).

lessons.text: When a clause states that the applicant must be a specific type of professional or individual, such as 'an Indian scientist working in agriculture', write a rule that confirms their professional status without adding unnecessary conditions.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies a professional requirement
lessons.review_note: Too vague to change behaviour.

lessons.text: A clause asking for a document, certificate or letter ("No Objection Certificate", "letter of acceptance") is something to submit: write no rule for it.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions a document requirement

lessons.text: When a clause specifies that an applicant must be the only girl child in the family, write a rule that checks if the applicant is a woman or girl.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'only girl child in the family'
lessons.review_note: Wrong and specific: C15 needs is_only_child, not only a gender check.

lessons.text: When a clause says only one person per family can benefit, write family_member_already_beneficiary eq false.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'only one person in the family'

lessons.text: When a benefit can be had only once ("eligible only once", "can be availed only once"), write a has_availed_<scheme>_before eq false rule.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies 'eligible only once during the course of study'

lessons.text: For former or present Ministers, MPs, MLAs, Mayors or District Panchayat chairpersons, use is_former_or_present_listed_political_office_holder when the clause is about the applicant, and family_has_former_or_present_listed_political_office_holder when it is about any family member.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions political office holders.

lessons.text: When a clause refers to total income, use 'annual_family_income' instead of 'annual_income'.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies total income from all sources.
lessons.review_note: Not general: C16 uses family income because of an official-source answer; C31's limit is applicant and spouse.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies eligibility based on gender for women scientists, use 'is_woman_or_girl' instead of 'is_permanent_employee'.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies eligibility for women scientists.
lessons.review_note: Doesn't follow from the error (C25's category field).

lessons.text: When a scheme specifies 'any' for eligibility, write the rule with 'or_conditions' to reflect that multiple conditions can be satisfied. If it specifies 'all', write the rule without 'or_conditions', indicating all conditions must be met.
lessons.applies_when: the clause indicates eligibility based on 'any' or 'all'.
flags: no specific keyword left, so it would be sent for every scheme
lessons.review_note: Confuses rule_logic (how rules combine) with or_conditions (alternatives inside one rule).

lessons.text: An age relaxation of X years for named groups is two rules. Example: upper age 35, relaxed by 5 years: (1) age lte 40, the relaxed limit, for everyone; (2) age lte 35, the normal limit, with or_conditions for each relaxed group (social_category in [...], is_woman_or_girl eq true, has_disability eq true).
lessons.applies_when: age relaxation is mentioned
lessons.review_note: Round 1 swapped the two limits in C24, C26 and M14.

lessons.text: When a clause lists several qualifying kinds of one requirement joined by EITHER/OR (courses, years of study, posts), write one rule for that requirement (a yes/no field, or field in [the kinds]), not one rule per kind.
lessons.applies_when: multiple student categories are listed
lessons.review_note: In C36 it produced the same condition twice as alternatives; no scheme improved.

lessons.text: 'BPL OR income up to Rs N' is one rule: household_below_bpl eq true, with or_conditions [the income field the clause names, lte N]. Use annual_family_income only when the clause says the family's income.
lessons.applies_when: BPL families or income limit is mentioned
lessons.review_note: Its example field spread into M12's applicant income rules.

lessons.text: When a clause states that an applicant 'must not exceed' a certain limit, write the rule with 'lte' using the specified limit. If it states 'must exceed', write 'gt' instead.
lessons.applies_when: a limit is phrased as 'must not exceed' or 'must exceed'.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a category or list of eligible conditions, ensure all specified conditions are included in the rule. If the clause lists multiple categories, write a rule that includes all of them.
lessons.applies_when: a clause lists multiple categories or conditions for eligibility.
lessons.review_note: Vague; L012 covers the useful part.

lessons.text: An exclusion clause (excl-, or "is not eligible") names who is excluded, so its rule requires the opposite: field eq false.
lessons.applies_when: a clause states that something is 'not eligible'.
lessons.review_note: Now sent for every scheme: it never reached M19, whose exclusions don't use its keywords.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a requirement for a specific profession or role (e.g., 'must be an Indian scientist', 'must be a Senior Citizen'), write a rule indicating that requirement as true.
lessons.applies_when: a clause specifies a profession or role requirement.
lessons.review_note: Generic; pushes towards more rules, the main error.

lessons.text: When a clause states that an applicant must have a specific interest or qualification (e.g., 'must have an insurable interest', 'must hold a Ph.D.'), write a rule indicating that interest or qualification as true.
lessons.applies_when: a clause specifies a required interest or qualification.
lessons.review_note: Generic; pushes towards more rules, the main error.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a condition that excludes certain individuals (e.g., 'the girl child will not be considered'), write a rule indicating that condition as false.
lessons.applies_when: a clause specifies an exclusion condition.
lessons.review_note: Covered by L016, now sent for every scheme.

lessons.text: 'Senior Citizen' means age gte 60.
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies a type of applicant

lessons.text: When a clause excludes people covered under other social security schemes and names them (NPS, ESIC, EPFO), write one eq false rule per named scheme: is_nps_member, is_esic_member, is_epfo_member.
lessons.applies_when: the clause mentions membership in other schemes

lessons.text: When a clause indicates that a specific status or condition must be true for eligibility (e.g., 'must possess a letter of acceptance'), write a rule that checks for that condition (e.g., 'has_paper_accepted_at_event_abroad eq true').
lessons.applies_when: the clause specifies a required status or condition
lessons.review_note: Generic.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a unique identifier for a rule (e.g., 'elig-2', 'elig-3'), ensure that the correct identifier is used in the rule. If the identifier in the draft does not match the gold standard, it indicates a wrong clause reference.
lessons.applies_when: the clause includes a specific eligibility identifier
lessons.review_note: Trivial.

lessons.text: When a clause refers to a specific group or category (e.g., 'only girl child', 'Medal winners of National games'), ensure that the rule accurately reflects the specific eligibility criteria without altering the intended meaning.
lessons.applies_when: the clause defines a specific group or category
lessons.review_note: Vague.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a type of income limit ('total income', 'annual income'), use 'annual_family_income' for family income limits, not 'annual_income'.
lessons.applies_when: an income limit clause
lessons.review_note: Repeats L008, rejected in round 1.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies a type of applicant ('Women Scientists', 'Persons who paid Income Tax'), use the appropriate field that directly relates to that applicant type, not a general field.
lessons.applies_when: a clause specifies a particular applicant type
lessons.review_note: Vague.

lessons.text: When a clause states that an applicant should not be receiving benefits from other schemes, use 'receives_other_government_housing_benefit' for housing schemes, not a general exclusion field.
lessons.applies_when: a clause about receiving benefits from other schemes
lessons.review_note: Memorises M12's field.

lessons.text: When a clause specifies that eligibility is determined by 'any' condition being met, write a rule that uses 'any' logic. If it specifies 'all', write a rule that uses 'all' logic instead.
lessons.applies_when: the clause indicates eligibility based on 'any' or 'all' conditions.
flags: no specific keyword left, so it would be sent for every scheme
lessons.review_note: Like rejected L010; would be sent for every scheme.

lessons.text: When a clause states a range (e.g., 'Age: 57-62 years'), write one rule for the lower limit and one for the upper limit, using 'gte' for the lower limit and 'lte' for the upper limit, and include an 'or_conditions' for any additional criteria.
lessons.applies_when: a range is specified
lessons.review_note: The range part is already in the instructions; the or_conditions part is wrong.

lessons.text: 'More than X' or 'above X' does not include X: use gt, not gte.
lessons.applies_when: a percentage threshold is specified

lessons.text: When a clause mentions multiple qualifying conditions (e.g., 'is recommended by the Zonal Cultural Centres, Ministry of Culture'), write one rule for each condition using 'or_conditions'.
lessons.applies_when: multiple qualifying conditions are mentioned
lessons.review_note: Vague (one scheme).

lessons.text: When a clause states 'Excluding' certain groups, write a rule that sets the corresponding field to false for those groups: field eq false.
lessons.applies_when: an exclusion clause that specifies groups or categories
lessons.review_note: Harmful: in C03 and M13 '(Excluding MTS / Class IV / Group D)' is an exception to an exclusion.

lessons.text: A caste or category requirement ('SC / ST', 'OBC', 'VJNT') is social_category in [the listed categories], spelled as in the field list; 'VJNT' means VJ-A, NT-B, NT-C and NT-D.
lessons.applies_when: a clause specifies categories of applicants

lessons.text: When a clause specifies an upper age limit and includes age relaxation for certain groups, write two rules: one for the upper limit and another for the relaxed age limit for each specified group.
lessons.applies_when: an upper age limit with age relaxation for specific groups
lessons.review_note: A vaguer copy of L011.
